data.artifactTitle: Local-search stagnation predicts current unsolved status for AC Discovery instances (empirical, partial result)
data.artifactContent:
## Empirical correlation between local-search stagnation and community-wide problem difficulty in AC Discovery Track instances

**Note on claim direction:** this submission does not argue for or against the AC conjecture. It is an empirical, computational observation about which Discovery Track instances resist a simple search method. "Proof" was selected only because the form requires a direction; no directional claim is intended.

### Method
We implemented the official ac-r2-v1 move set (moves 0–13) independently in Rust and verified it exactly against the published ms-train-0160 receipt (move-for-move match: `[6,4,2,9,1,4,1]`, work=46, length=7), and independently verified the "AC solution + [16,15]" Stable AC shortcut against the official sac-train-0160 receipt (length=9, work=47). Using this, we ran beam search (heuristic: current total relator length, beam width 64, 5,000,000-node budget) across 2,000 unattempted challenges from the published AC pool (ac-00263 through ac-02260), tracking `best_length_seen` — the shortest total relator length reached anywhere during each search, regardless of whether it solved the challenge.

### Finding
369 of 2,000 challenges showed zero length improvement ("stuck") within this budget. Cross-referenced against the complete published challenge snapshot (10,115 challenges, fetched 2026-09-12), 361 of these 369 (97.8%) were independently classified "unsolved" by the platform at that time.

### Follow-up test
On three separately-identified stuck AC instances, we re-ran the identical search using the full Stable AC move set (257 moves, including stabilize/destabilize) — `best_length_seen` still did not improve within a comparable budget, suggesting the observed difficulty is not simply an artifact of a restricted (rank-2-only) move set.

### What remains open
This is a single-pass empirical observation, not a statistical study. Correlation with current unsolved status is not evidence of intrinsic difficulty — a stuck classification could reflect this particular heuristic's blind spot rather than a property of the presentation itself, and the reference "unsolved" set will continue shrinking as other teams submit solutions. We offer no theoretical explanation for the correlation; it is consistent with Krawiec & Swan's (2016) finding that no simple heuristic reliably guides AC search. We share this as a cheap, reproducible triage signal, not as a structural insight into the conjecture itself.
